key_insight: All tested URANS models capture key start-up quantities, but RSM better resolves trailing-edge and draft-tube frequency content by consistently capturing turbulence anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: Computationally tractable start-up CFD can support variable-speed pump-turbine design as frequent start-stop cycles increase fatigue loading and threaten runner lifetime.
method: Simulate a linear start-up of a variable-speed reversible pump-turbine using transient CFD.
Compare URANS approaches using k–ω SST, EARSM, and RSM turbulence models.
Evaluate torque, mass flow, and frequency content at blade edges and in the draft tube.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate torque, mass flow, and leading-edge blade-passing frequency content for all models, with substantially better trailing-edge and draft-tube frequency resolution using RSM.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative error metrics or computational costs, limiting assessment of the accuracy–cost trade-off.
paper_title: Transient CFD simulation of a linear start-up of a variable speed reversible pump-turbine
